title: Raising the Bar: A Year of Progress for EA Javelin Anticheat
summary: 57.1 million players safeguarded across our ecosystem, 26.7 million cheat attempts prevented, and more
body_markdown:
Since launching EA Javelin Anticheat in September 2022, we've continued to raise the bar for PC game security. This past year marked significant expansion and refinement as we worked to protect more players, improve performance, and took our enforcement efforts beyond the game client.


## The Last Year, By The Numbers


Since[our last report](https://www.ea.com/news/anticheat-progress-report) , we've expanded our reach and pushed EA Javelin Anticheat to operate at a much larger scale. Here's a look at what it took to defend our player base over the past year:


- **20 titles** now protected
- **57.1 million players** safeguarded across our ecosystem
- **26.7 million cheat attempts** prevented
- **99%+ accuracy rate** in cheat detection
- **<1% stability error rate**
- **Hundreds** of features, updates, and bug fixes deployed
- **60% faster game launch times**


## Faster, Smoother, Better


We know every second counts when you want to play. This year, we cut EA Javelin Anticheat launch times in half through optimized startup processes. We also upgraded our anti-tampering system, achieving 20% faster performance and a 10% smaller footprint.


Players now see progress indicators during launch and get clearer error messages in all EA-supported languages when something needs attention. We enforce minimum Windows requirements upfront with helpful guidance rather than cryptic errors.


We fixed multiple compatibility issues with AMD and NVIDIA driver updates, ensuring features like AMD Anti-Lag, NVIDIA Smooth Motion, and DLSS over-the-air updates work seamlessly with EA Javelin Anticheat. When we deployed a compatibility fix for AMD Anti-Lag in October 2025, it resolved launch issues for 45,000 players within 48 hours…and most never even knew there was a problem.


Behind the scenes, we completed a major backend infrastructure migration with zero player disruption. That is a testament to our engineering discipline.


## Securing the PC Ecosystem


EA Javelin Anticheat’s impact extends beyond individual games. This year, **over 4.8M players enabled Secure Boot** on their systems after we introduced configurable Secure Boot requirements, starting with Battlefield 2042. This industry-leading approach strengthens the entire PC gaming ecosystem against kernel-level threats.


For Battlefield 6, we also introduced TPM 2.0 requirements, establishing a new security baseline for next-generation titles.


## Taking the Fight Outside the Game


EA raised concerns with Collective Minds, the manufacturer of the Cronus Zen and Strike Pack hardware devices, regarding third-party tools that enable cheating in multiple EA titles. Following our engagement, EA-related content and scripts were removed from the Cronus Zen and Strike Pack public sites and Discord server.


## Evolving Threat Detection


In the past year, we’ve deployed hundreds of detection updates, targeting evolving cheat methods:


- **Anti-DMA protection** : New capabilities to detect and block Direct Memory Access cheat hardware
- **Input manipulation defense** : Multiple updates blocking malicious input devices, macro software, and synthetic input tools
- **Continuous adaptation** : 7 major security upgrades plus hundreds of incremental improvements


Cheat providers often advertise “undetectable” status, a claim that's always temporary. We see cheat subscriptions averaging $20-150/month, creating a lucrative black market we're working to dismantle through technical, legal, and platform partnership approaches.


## New Titles, New Challenges


Over the past year, EA Javelin Anticheat expanded to protect some of EA's biggest launches and experiences, including skate., Battlefield Labs, Battlefield 6, and EA SPORTS College Football 27. Each title brings unique gameplay mechanics and threat models, requiring tailored detection strategies while maintaining our ecosystem-wide learnings.


## The Trade-Offs We Make


We balance detection speed with accuracy. We could ban more, faster, but we’d risk false positives impacting our legitimate players. Every new detection must clear a high bar: effective against cheaters without impacting legitimate play styles or accessibility tools.


We maintain an appeals process for players who believe they were banned in error. Our review process is thorough but we don't disclose specifics to prevent exploitation. Our <1% false positive rate reflects our commitment to accuracy.


We operate at kernel level because detecting external cheats requires it, not because we want deeper access. Javelin only runs when a game with Javelin protection included is running. All anti-cheat processes shut down when the game does. And, if you have uninstalled all of your EA games that have Javelin protection, Javelin will automatically uninstall and remove itself from your PC.


## What's Next


In the near future, EA Javelin Anticheat will offer native ARM64 support. Whether you're on traditional x86 hardware or a next-gen ARM-based Windows device, you'll get the same great experience with no compromises. Stay tuned for more details.


The cat-and-mouse game with cheaters never stops. Neither do we. We continually invest in R&D, machine learning models, behavioral analysis, and deeper, hardware-level protections. Our goal is to make cheating in EA titles so difficult, so expensive, and so risky, that it's not worth the effort.
